title: Shiva, the goddess and a book with a reputation
hookLine: set the rumor down and open an actual Tantra
carry: the world is shakti, the goddess's own power
tomorrow: anyone can read a Tantra. so why does it say reading isn't enough?
last: NOT AWAY FROM THE WORLD, BUT THROUGH IT.

lines: HOW CAN SUFFERING BEINGS BE FREED?
cards: Say the word tantra at a party and sometimes people smirk. Online it sells weekend workshops and racy book covers. So set the rumor down for a minute and open an actual Tantra.
The Kularnava Tantra begins on a mountain. The goddess turns to Shiva with a question about beings caught in the round of birth and death, suffering, unable to find a way out. How can they be freed?

teach.b: So what is tantra, actually? Start plain. A Tantra, with a capital T, is a book, a sacred text, one of a family of them.
The ones this run visits are framed as conversations between Shiva and the goddess, one asking, one answering.

Then look at what fills the pages: how a student receives a mantra from a teacher, how to draw a sacred diagram, how to worship the goddess or Shiva step by step, how to meditate on the divine within the body.
The stuff of worship. Beneath it sits a way of seeing, as tantric teachers describe it: the world isn't a trap to climb out of.

teach.h: THE WORLD AS THE GODDESS'S POWER.
teach.b: Its energy is Shakti, the goddess's own power, so the path runs through ordinary life, body and all. A Jewish neighbor would recognize one piece of that.

teach.h: ECCLESIASTES: EAT THY BREAD WITH JOY.
teach.b: Ecclesiastes says: 'Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy.' Ordinary life, bread and all, received as good. That much is shared.
The honest difference: in Ecclesiastes the joy is a gift of the one God, who has already accepted your works, as the verse goes on to say.
The Tantras speak of the world as Shakti, and build a whole practice of mantra, diagram and meditation on it.
So for the coming days the word carries three meanings: a kind of book, the practices it teaches, and the way of seeing they grow from.

how: Tantric texts and practices shape worship in several Hindu traditions, Shaiva and Shakta especially, and some temple rites draw on the related Agamas.

games.q: what does “what tantra actually is” mean?
o: a family of sacred books on worship, mantra and meditation
a set of love poems written for married couples
a school of fortune-telling from the stars

games.q: the book, not the rumor — tap the pairs.
p: a sacred book, framed as a dialogue
how can bound beings be freed?

s: the Tantras' pages are full of mantra, worship, sacred diagrams and meditation.
the Kularnava Tantra opens with a question about how suffering beings can be freed
the goddess asks, and Shiva answers.
Ecclesiastes and the Tantras say the same thing about ordinary life
both receive ordinary life as good; Ecclesiastes as a gift of the one God, the Tantras as the goddess's power.

games.q: a classmate's slide calls tantra 'the spicy side of yoga.' you're asked to suggest one fix. what's the most accurate place to start?
o: open an actual Tantra and say what fills its pages.
drop the topic; it's too awkward for class.
keep the slide; the reputation is what tantra is.
games.why: a Tantra is a sacred book, framed as a dialogue of Shiva and the goddess, full of mantra, worship, diagrams and meditation.

practice: Sit upright, palms resting on your knees, and let your attention travel slowly from your feet to the top of your head. Don't fix anything; just notice the body as a place you're living in right now.
If you pray, you can let that noticing be your prayer.
